Title: 又 (yòu) vs. 再 (zài): "Again" in the Past vs. Future | Confusing Chinese Words Chart
Description: Both mean "again", but they look in opposite directions in time! Use 又 (yòu) for an action that has ALREADY happened again in the past (e.g. 他又迟到了 "He is late again"). Use 再 (zài) for an action that will happen again in the FUTURE (e.g. 请再说一次 "Please say it again", 再见 "see you again"). Title: 多少 (duōshao) vs. 几 (jǐ): Asking "How Many" in Chinese | Confusing Chinese Words Chart
Description: Use 几 (jǐ) when the expected quantity is small (typically less than 10), and a measure word is MANDATORY (e.g. 几个人, 几本书). Use 多少 (duōshao) for quantities over 10 or unknown amounts (prices, phone numbers), and the measure word is OPTIONAL (e.g. 多少(个)人, 多少钱).
